title: First Unique Number
statement:
A stream of customer visits arrives one at a time. Each customer has a positive integer id. A customer is a **one-time visitor** if they have visited exactly **once** so far.

Support two operations:

- `post x`: record a visit by customer `x`.
- `query`: report the one-time visitor whose **first visit came earliest**. If nobody is currently a one-time visitor, report `-1`.

A customer who has visited two or more times is never a one-time visitor again, even if later visits stop. Operations are processed in the order given; for each `query` print one line with its answer.

**Follow-up:** make both `post` and `query` run in `O(1)` (amortized is acceptable for a queue that prunes duplicates lazily; a hash map plus a doubly linked list gives worst-case `O(1)`). Discuss the trade-off between the two designs.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `q`, the number of operations.
Each of the next `q` lines is either `post x` or `query`.
outputFormat: For every `query`, print one line with its answer. Print the answers in the order the queries appear.
constraints: The input contains at least one `query`

hints: A hash map from id to visit count tells you instantly whether an id is a one-time visitor. The remaining question is how to find the earliest one quickly.
Keep a queue of ids in order of their first visit. When a query arrives, look at the front: if its count is above 1 it can never be a one-time visitor again, so pop it and look at the next.

Each id enters the queue once and leaves it at most once, so the total pruning work across all queries is O(q). A doubly linked list with a hash map of nodes lets you delete a duplicate the moment its second visit arrives instead.

        return str(len(ops)) + '\n' + '\n'.join(ops)
    P = lambda x: 'post ' + str(x)
    Q = 'query'
    tests = [fmt([Q]), fmt([P(1), Q]), fmt([P(1), P(1), Q]), fmt([P(7), P(8), P(7), Q, P(8), Q, P(9), Q]),
             fmt([P(10**9), Q, P(10**9), Q, P(1), Q]), fmt([Q, P(3), Q, Q, P(3), Q])]
    for _ in range(24):
        n = rng.randint(1, 30)

        ops = [Q if rng.random() < 0.3 else P(rng.randint(1, hi)) for _ in range(n)]
        ops.append(Q)
        tests.append(fmt(ops))
    ops = [P(i) for i in range(1, 16001)] + [P(i) for i in range(1, 16000)] + [Q] * 18000
    tests.append(fmt(ops))
    ops = []

        ops.append(P(i))

        ops.append(Q)
